title: A repeated common respiration history fits five North Pacific oxygen records within 3.05 micromol/kg under fixed exponential renewal
abstract: We test whether repeated respiration changes remove the mismatch of a single permanent rate step in five North Pacific oxygen records on density 26.5. We fit one annual rate history to all five regions with fixed exponential renewal and free fixed regional offsets. A bounded nonnegative total rate fits 35 five-year block means within 3.049 micromol/kg. The best tested baseline scale is 8 micromol/kg/year, the upper edge of the tested range. This existence result is below the earlier 7.243 single-step lower error bound. Near-best fits require rapid rate changes. At a 5 micromol/kg error allowance, a least-variable solution has total rates of 5.86-13.22 micromol/kg/year. Unrestricted signed rates fit the blocks exactly but are physically invalid. Annual observations need much larger errors. Holding the input constant for ten years gives a 7.19 micromol/kg error, so most of the improvement requires short-term rate changes. These are in-sample scenario fits, not measured respiration rates, statistical rejection, or a causal attribution. Sparse observations, fixed independent boxes and an assumed AOU-to-renewal scale limit inference. Code, input hashes, rate histories and independent optimality checks are included.
